sources.entry: CyTube - Synchronize media, chat, and more for an arbitrary number of channels. (Demo) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: CyTube is a self-hostable web application for synchronized video watching, with a shared playlist and chatroom per channel, built on Node.js and released under the MIT license.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes CyTube as a clone of the defunct synchtube.com, started as a hobby project in early 2013. Users register channels where connected viewers watch videos from various video hosts (the README gives YouTube and Twitch as examples) with playback synchronized across everyone in the channel. Each channel has a playlist that viewers can queue videos into, plus an integrated chatroom. The README notes an official server exists and that other public servers are run by various communities. Installation instructions for server administrators are on the project wiki rather than in the README itself.
use_cases: host a community video watch party
run a shared playlist with chat
collaborative video queue for a community
how_to_run: See the installation guide for server administrators on the project wiki (linked from the README; not included in the README text).
notable: Synchronized playback of videos from multiple video hosts across all viewers in a channel
Per-channel playlist where viewers queue videos
Clone of the defunct synchtube.com service
caveats: Installation details are on an external wiki, not in the README
README does not state specific supported video hosts beyond examples (YouTube, Twitch)
keywords: host my own watch party server
